what_happened: Scene layout 2 / style 2: dark single sink with a dish rack, faucet with a vertical stick lever, potted plant behind; iceberg lettuce (Lettuce008) in a perforated colander right of the sink. Stage 0 slowish: the gripper hovered near the lever ~100-394 (wrist: lever and the plant), touched it 394-445 and water came on at 439 (median 253, p90 449). Stage 1: colander grasped at 601 (width 0.038), carried into the basin 650-700 next to the stream. At ~703 the fingers closed further (0.038 -> 0.003): the colander slipped out and dropped onto the basin floor (716-724), the lettuce rolled out of it and came to rest right under the stream (wrist 724-744 shows the stream hitting the lettuce). Success at 742 (303 steps).
self_recovery: The colander slipped from the gripper at ~703, but the lettuce fell out under the stream, so the slip produced the success rather than being recovered from. Partly lucky.

packet_facts: close_events 601 (0.038, touching+lifting lettuce = colander grasp), 703 (0.003, nothing: colander slipped)

uncertain_about: Whether the drop at ~703 was a slip (width went down, not up, so the fingers did not open) or a squeeze that tipped the colander; either way the lettuce landed under the stream.
